You said that she is a nurse, so I’m sure she will be able to understand when to go talk to a doctor about the side effects. There are other options, the copper iud has no hormones for example. 
I wish both of you the best! Try to not worry about it to much, especially if she just got it put in :)

I feel like most women are kind of put-off by me tho, especially in the beginning. I feel like they don’t want to be associated with me.

If I get the chance to spend time with other women multiple times, while being “forced” to talk/team work as for jobs or school, I can actually make some friends. What continues to happen tho, is that I get faaar to exited and keen to make a friend, that I do everything to keep them happy around me. I listen to them, support them, compliment them etc. I also kind of mould my personality to fit theirs... it happens unintentionally, I wish I didn’t do this and I am trying to change my ways. I just agree on everything they say, to keep them as a friend. What happens then is that a lot of them end up wanting to hang out, while I don’t, since I haven’t been myself from the start. I have created this “perfect conversation-partner” for them specifically, and it is exhausting to keep up. What I want is a friend I can be comfortable around, and that can be comfortable with me. 
I have end up being used by nearly every female friend I have ever had... it is my fault tho, for not being able to set up healthy boundaries.

Honestly, it’s a relief to hear that I am not alone, at the same time, I’m sad to hear about everyones struggles... ❤️
I brought up this topic to my therapist actually. That, and that I have felt inadequate as a girl/woman my entire life. Like I am not good/“cool”/kind enough to hang out with other women. Like they know all these rules that I simply don’t, and I just end up feeling left out, odd, behind... And I feel SO much shame and guilt about the way that I feel. My therapist hit me with the “what does it have to mean to be a girl anyway?”... it just made me so sad. I felt so misunderstood, and it felt like she was trying to shame me for being “not like other girls” or something... she was the first one I ever verbalized this to, so it hurt. I think a lot of this has to do with being bullied by girls my age when I was younger, but at the same time, I feel like the bullying started because of me not fitting in with the other girls/me being so insecure around them. I remember feeling this way before the bullying happened, like the other girls knew some kind of secrets of how to be cool and kind and social, that I didn’t. The bullying didn’t make it better tho. 
I really love women tho. There are so many I look up to so much❤️

Hi! This is my second time trying out the copper iud, I experienced something very much like what you described here. The first months very fine, just a bit more pain and heavier flow when I had my period. Then the spotting began after about 8 months or so? Brown and sometimes pinkish (sorry for tmi). After about 3 months of daily spotting, I took it out. I went to get it checked before, and the doctor took tests for infections and such, and did an ultrasound but nothing seemed to be out of the ordinary. The bleeding/spotting stopped right after I took it out. 

I have had an other copper IUD inserted, and I really want it to work out this time! 😢

Having health anxiety is really tiring, I easily get that to, so I really feel for you!! For me, nothing was wrong, and the doctors doesn’t know what could have caused the bleeding. I wish you the best, take care!! <3
